'''RamapoCon II''' was a Star Wars CCG constructed championship on 6 May 2000 at a student center. [[Scott Lingrell]] directed the event. [[Rich Haman]] ran it with him. 66 players entered. [[Jonny Chu]] defeated [[Chris Terwilliger]] in the final duel.<ref name="ramapo2000">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-05-13-ramapocon-ii-day-2-director-s-reportd741/ RamapoCon II Day 2 Director's Report], Scott Lingrell, DeckTech (13 May 2000).</ref>

* '''Tournament director:''' [[Scott Lingrell]]<ref name="ramapo2000">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-05-13-ramapocon-ii-day-2-director-s-reportd741/ RamapoCon II Day 2 Director's Report], Scott Lingrell, DeckTech (13 May 2000).</ref>

[[Bart Robinson]] helped with setup and entered game 2 to stop a bye. Blythe Hermley-Keen ran the computer.<ref name="ramapo2000">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-05-13-ramapocon-ii-day-2-director-s-reportd741/ RamapoCon II Day 2 Director's Report], Scott Lingrell, DeckTech (13 May 2000).</ref>

== Results ==

After six Swiss games [[Chris Terwilliger]] led on 12(+107). Chu was second on 10(+88) and won the final duel.<ref name="ramapo2000">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-05-13-ramapocon-ii-day-2-director-s-reportd741/ RamapoCon II Day 2 Director's Report], Scott Lingrell, DeckTech (13 May 2000).</ref>

== Side events ==

A Young Jedi event ran in the morning. [[Chris Gogolen]] directed it. [[Doug Faust]] was the highest 3–1 player.<ref name="ramapo2000">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-05-13-ramapocon-ii-day-2-director-s-reportd741/ RamapoCon II Day 2 Director's Report], Scott Lingrell, DeckTech (13 May 2000).</ref>

[[Ted Panczyszyn]] ran an Austin Powers event (6 players). Dan Bordier won.<ref name="ramapo2000">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-05-13-ramapocon-ii-day-2-director-s-reportd741/ RamapoCon II Day 2 Director's Report], Scott Lingrell, DeckTech (13 May 2000).</ref>

A No Such Thing As Luck event had 12 players. Bob Caton won.<ref name="ramapo2000">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-05-13-ramapocon-ii-day-2-director-s-reportd741/ RamapoCon II Day 2 Director's Report], Scott Lingrell, DeckTech (13 May 2000).</ref>

Faust directed a three-game booster-draft sealed event with 36 players. Chris Erwin finished first.<ref name="ramapo2000">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-05-13-ramapocon-ii-day-2-director-s-reportd741/ RamapoCon II Day 2 Director's Report], Scott Lingrell, DeckTech (13 May 2000).</ref>

[[Kevin Reitzel]] of Decipher played in the constructed championship.<ref name="ramapo2000">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-05-13-ramapocon-ii-day-2-director-s-reportd741/ RamapoCon II Day 2 Director's Report], Scott Lingrell, DeckTech (13 May 2000).</ref>

== Decklists ==
Players posted these lists on DeckTech as decks they played at the event; the posted list may differ slightly from the one played.

* [[RamapoCon II Charlie Herren Ungarmax]] ([[Charlie Herren]], [[Dark]]; 7–2) — "the Huntdown deck I played at RamapoCon, going a combined 7-2 in the first 2 days"
